snippet: (sweep over context_lines in {8,20,40,60,80,whole} x 3 repeats, 14 fixtures, qwen-2.5-7b)
note: def 37 lines above sink; non-monotonic accuracy curve
observed: good-rate: cl8=5.6% cl20=0.0%(worst, dangerous under-flags) cl40=80.6% cl60=91.7%(0 unstable) cl80=91.7% whole=91.7%
lesson: Raise DEFAULT_CONTEXT_LINES from 8 to 60. Threshold = function-scope (def->sink distance ~37 lines): below it the cheap model guesses instead of returning uncertain. cl=20 is the worst setting (partial-context valley produces confident WRONG verdicts incl. dangerous under-flags). cl=60 is smallest fully-stable window at the 92% plateau. Residual 8% (env_injection LD_PRELOAD literal over-flag) is a prompt artifact for #96, not fixable by window size. Total LLM spend $0.0104.

note: context-window sweep headline; full report reports/security-scan-calibration/20260524_071656+0200-context-window-sweep.md
observed: good-rate vs cl on qwen-2.5-7b: cl8=5.6%, cl20=0.0% (DANGEROUS valley, 10/36 under-flags), cl40=80.6%, cl60=91.7% (0 unstable, smallest stable), cl80=91.7%, whole=91.7%. Off-window the model abstained only 2/72 — it GUESSES. spend $0.0104.
lesson: DEFAULT_CONTEXT_LINES bumped 8→60 (types.ts). Accuracy is non-monotonic; partial context (cl=20) is MORE dangerous than tiny (cl=8). Cheap model does NOT abstain on missing provenance → mitigation is an adequate window, not abstention. Surface-only categories are window-insensitive (lower cl OK); taint/provenance categories need ≥60. Residual ~8% = env_injection LD_PRELOAD literal over-flag (window-invariant prompt artifact, separate issue).

note: TRDD-973a0265 curated this corpus into mcp-server/src/benchmark/security-triage/dataset.jsonl (33 self-contained snippet cases)
observed: BUILT: dataset.ts (loader + BENCHMARK_RUBRICS + per-tool SECURITY_TRIAGE_CRITERIA: structured-output + modest-ctx, NO reasoning/128K) + score.ts (+1 correct / -1 under-flag / 0 else; PASS = zero critical under-flags AND score>=0.5) + runner.ts (reuses judgeGroups) + select.ts (requirements + benchmark-pass + never-pricier, best-of-equivalent-cost) + index.ts orchestrator (discover->run->score->gate->report, per-model-per-day cache). 3 surfaces: MCP security_triage_benchmark / CLI llm-ext-benchmark --security-triage / slash command. 34 offline unit tests + 1 live e2e; full 742-test suite green.
lesson: minScore=0.5 calibrated so qwen-2.5-7b (~92% good at cl=60 per #95) passes as baseline while a broad under-flagger fails. Off-window-uncertain cases score (reward abstention) but are NOT in the mandatory floor (the cheap model can't reliably abstain). The corpus is the source of truth; dataset.jsonl is the curated runnable subset — append new cases here first, then curate.

note: discovered during #96 live validation: judge.ts cleared the per-call abort timeout right after fetch resolved HEADERS, leaving await res.json()/res.text() unbounded
expected: every judge call bounded by per_call_timeout_ms (request AND body)
observed: a provider that returns 200 then streams/stalls the body hung the call indefinitely (3 consecutive live runs hung 4-15min on a degraded qwen provider). FIX: keep the abort timer armed through the body read (res.json/res.text are tied to controller.signal), clear on every exit path. Regression test added (security_scan.test.ts: hung RESPONSE BODY fail-safes within the timeout).
lesson: A timeout that only covers the request, not the response-body read, is a slow-loris hang vector — serious in a SECURITY tool. Always bound the FULL request+body. NOTE: fetchProgrammingModels (discover.ts catalog fetch) still has no timeout — future hardening.

note: the first COMPLETE live run scored qwen 0.242 FAIL with under=0/over=0/critUF=0 — because ~25/33 calls timed out (degraded qwen provider) and fail-safed to uncertain, which the scorer counted as wrong answers
expected: a degraded network/provider must NOT falsely fail a good model
observed: FIX: the scorer now EXCLUDES fail-safe (errored) verdicts from scoring; a run with >15% errored calls (maxErrorRate) is INCONCLUSIVE — neither pass nor fail, excluded from selection, incumbent kept. qwen's REAL verdicts still clear the critical floor.
lesson: A model-qualification benchmark MUST distinguish a model's verdict from an infrastructure fail-safe. Scoring timeouts as wrong answers makes the gate untrustworthy (false-negatives reject good models, or could switch away from a sound incumbent). Operational: qwen-2.5-7b's OpenRouter provider was degraded 2026-05-24 while gemini/gpt-5.4-nano responded fine — re-run the live aggregate when qwen is healthy.

note: 3-model triage assessment 2026-05-24 (qwen + gemini-2.5-flash + grok-4.1-fast, --force) to decide #9/#10 with data
expected: determine whether the #9/#10 edge cases are model-solvable, and at what cost
observed: gemini-2.5-flash PASS score=0.909 scored=33/33 errored=0 under=0 critUF=0 — handled the EXACT #9/#10 cases: pi-detection-classifier-src->uncertain (acceptable), pt-static-literal->not_threat, pt-provenance-off-window->uncertain, redir-off-window->uncertain, env-onwindow-static->not_threat; its only 3 misses (pt-onwindow-static, sqli-off-window, fswrite-in-doc) were all SAFE-direction over-cautious (0 under-flags). qwen INCONCLUSIVE (32/33 errored, provider still degraded). grok-4.1-fast INCONCLUSIVE (33/33 errored). spend $0.0142.
lesson: DECISION (with data): the #9/#10 prompt+rubric fixes are CORRECT — a capable model following the SAME prompt nails the edge cases, so the residual is purely qwen's (cheapest model's) capacity, not a code bug. gemini-2.5-flash ($0.15/$0.60, ~5x qwen) is now the documented RECOMMENDED higher-accuracy triage model (proven PASS 0.909, 0 under-flags). Same-cost rule stands: default stays qwen, no auto-bump. #9/#10 resolved = code fixed + recommended model documented + benchmark gate is the standing re-qualification mechanism.
